edges.reason: transfer uses msg.sender as the source account for _transfer.
transferFrom indexes _allowed with msg.sender as spender.
approve stores allowance keyed by msg.sender.
approveAndCall forwards msg.sender to the receiveApproval callback.
burn debits _balances[msg.sender].
mint authorizes the caller by comparing msg.sender with owner.
burnFrom uses msg.sender as the approved spender.
acceptOwnership compares msg.sender with newOwner to grant ownership.
Owned constructor sets owner from msg.sender.
transferOwnership is restricted because owner gates the onlyOwner guard.
mint compares msg.sender against stored owner state variable.
acceptOwnership reads newOwner to authorize the caller.
transferOwnership writes the newOwner state variable.
transferOwnership is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier.
onlyOwner requires msg.sender to equal owner.
acceptOwnership performs the newOwner equality check.
mint executes the msg.sender == owner requirement.
approveAndCall performs an external call to the spender contract configured by the caller.
The external receiveApproval callback executes after the allowance stored in _allowed is updated, allowing reentrant state use.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external call on the caller-supplied token address.
The rescue external call sends tokens to the owner address.
approveAndCall invokes approve before the external callback.
transfer delegates the balance movement to _transfer.
transferFrom delegates the balance movement to _transfer.
transferFrom decrements the _allowed allowance value.
burn decrements balances and totalSupply.
mint increments totalSupply and the recipient balance with an overflow require.
burnFrom decrements balance, allowance and totalSupply.
_transfer adds and subtracts balances and asserts the invariant.
balanceOf reads _balances.
allowance reads _allowed.
_transfer reads and writes _balances.
transferFrom reads _allowed for the allowance check.
approve writes _allowed.
burn reduces totalSupply.
mint increases totalSupply.
burnFrom reduces totalSupply.
CommonToken constructor sets totalSupply from the initial supply.
CommonToken constructor assigns the name state variable.
CommonToken constructor assigns the symbol state variable.
CommonToken constructor assigns the decimals state variable.
CommonToken constructor credits _balances[msg.sender] with the whole supply.
burn mutates the caller balance entry.
mint mutates the recipient balance entry.
burnFrom mutates the target balance entry.
recipient parameter determines the balance credit in mint.
amount parameter determines the minted quantity.
amount parameter feeds the totalSupply addition in mint.
tokens parameter is forwarded to the rescue external call.
tokenAddress parameter determines the external callee of the rescue call.
_extraData parameter is forwarded to receiveApproval.
_spender parameter is cast to TokenRecipient and called.
_from parameter selects the account burned in burnFrom.
_value parameter sets the burn amount in burnFrom.
_value parameter feeds the subtractions performed in burnFrom.
previousBalances local is used in the _transfer invariant assertion.
_to parameter is the destination of the internal transfer.
_value parameter is the amount moved by the internal transfer.

normalization_plan.reason: recipient is only used to credit _balances inside mint, so it collapses into the mint function node.
amount exists solely as the mint quantity and merges into mint and its arithmetic node.
tokens is only an argument to the outgoing external transfer call in transferAnyERC20Token.
tokenAddress selects the callee of the rescue external call and has no standalone semantics.
_extraData is only forwarded to the callback in approveAndCall.
_spender only determines the callback target contract in approveAndCall.
_from is only used to index balances and allowances inside burnFrom.
_value is only the burn quantity inside burnFrom.
previousBalances is a transient local used only for the assertion inside _transfer.
_to is only the destination account inside the internal transfer routine.
_value is only the amount moved by the internal transfer routine.
